claims.quote: We can see that the performance of ProphetNetbase -3gram and ProphetNetbase -2gram is comparable. Both of them perform better than MASSbase and ProphetNetbase -1gram.
claims.reason: Authors explicitly call future n-gram prediction a novel self-supervised objective (abstract and §2). Table 6 compares n=1/2/3 and MASS at matched 6-layer size, Wiki+BookCorpus data, and 125k steps, so the objective is ablated with vs without multi-token future prediction.

Abstract and §2 present n-stream self-attention as their proposed extension of XLNet two-stream attention, a distinct ARCH contribution from the loss. Table 5 compares full ProphetNet to a Transformer at matched hyperparameters, but the gap also includes the n-gram loss and positional changes, so the comparison is confounded.

Token-span mask denoising is not stated as new: §2.4 says the denoising task is widely used and token span masking is the same as MASS. It is an adopted prior objective, not an ARCH/TRAIN novelty claim.

Same TRAIN contribution as A_only0 (future n-gram prediction for planning / less local overfitting), not a second claim. Its ablation=NO is also unsupported: Table 6 is a matched n-gram comparison, already coded YES on A_only0.
